candidates.title: Affordable, manageable, practical, and scalable (AMPS) high-yield and high-gain inertial fusion
candidates.notes: April 2025 preprint (Sandia/collaborators). Covers DS (Demonstration System) architecture targeting 60+ MA and net facility gain by 2030. Claims 1000x improvement over NIF at 1/10 capital cost. Full text accessible. Directly addresses the DS machine concept as the successor to Z-IFE LTD architecture.

candidates.title: Magnetized liner inertial fusion platform development to assess performance scaling with drive parameters
candidates.notes: Physics of Plasmas March 2025 peer-reviewed paper on MagLIF experimental scaling. OSTI page (osti.gov/biblio/2526283) may have free access. Not triaged further due to extraction budget allocation.

candidates.title: Pacific Fusion predicts '1,000-fold leap' in performance, net facility gain by 2030
candidates.notes: ANS Nuclear Newswire summary article. Likely repeats content from Pacific Fusion corporate announcement already extracted in iter-03. Not extracted.

gaps_attempted.notes: arXiv AMPS paper provides DS architecture concept and 60+ MA scaling claims, but does not constitute a full plant engineering or TEA study — it is a physics case paper, not a cost model. The ±50%+ driver capital uncertainty noted in the gap remains unresolved; no public cost breakdown for the IMG/DS architecture found.

candidates.title: Magnetization and Heating Tools for Low-Cost Fusion | ARPA-E
candidates.notes: ARPA-E project page for heating/magnetization tools, not driver capital cost. Not fetched further.

gaps_attempted.notes: No publicly accessible source found with specific IMG driver capital cost estimates at 60+ MA scale. ARPA-E award search did not surface IMG-specific cost data. Gap remains proprietary — Pacific Fusion's investor documents and DOE grant filings are not publicly accessible. The AMPS arXiv paper (extracted for G-1) makes a qualitative '1/10 capital cost' claim vs. NIF but provides no cost breakdown for the LTD/IMG pulsed-power architecture itself.

gaps_attempted.gap_description: Thermal cycle above 900 K: high-temperature materials availability for He Brayton or combined cycle
queries: ODS ferritic steel SiC composite fusion reactor blanket 900K thermal efficiency He Brayton cycle material availability

candidates.title: Assessment of structural materials in compact fusion reactor design
candidates.notes: Open-access 2025 paper in Frontiers in Nuclear Engineering. Covers ODS steels and SiC/SiC composites for compact fusion. Operating temperatures: ITER ~750K, DEMO ~570K, STEP ~670K, ARC ~850K. ODS identified as 'most promising candidates for high-temperature compact fusion devices.' Does not specifically discuss He Brayton cycle compatibility or >900K operation for MagLIF, but provides the best available open-access materials survey for this gap.

gaps_attempted.notes: Extracted paper provides relevant ODS/SiC materials context but focuses on ARC-class tokamak (~850K FLiBe blanket) rather than Z-pinch chamber at >900K. The gap asks specifically about He Brayton cycle and C-C composite availability above 900K for MagLIF thermal BOP; the Frontiers paper's thermal efficiency analysis does not directly address this. The z-ife-sand2006-7148-thermal-cycles source (iter-02) remains the primary thermal cycle reference for MagLIF; this new source supplements it with materials TRL context.

candidates.notes: Covers 60+ MA scaling and DS net facility gain target. The self-magnetizing target concept (eliminating external coils and laser) is related work — the experimental breakthrough (already in iter-03 sources) described this, while the AMPS paper covers the physics scaling case for the DS machine.

candidates.title: Pacific Fusion experimental breakthrough
candidates.notes: Already present as pacificfusion-updates-experimental-breakthrough-by-pacific in iter-03/sources. Describes self-magnetizing target eliminating external coils. Laser preheat elimination stated as 'next iteration' — not yet demonstrated.

gaps_attempted.notes: AMPS arXiv paper covers the DS machine scaling physics case. However, specific gain data for self-magnetizing targets at 60+ MA has not yet been experimentally published — the Pacific Fusion breakthrough paper (iter-03) covers the concept at 22 MA on Z. Full gain characterization awaits future DS-scale experiments (2030 target).

candidates.title: Fusion transmutation of waste: design and analysis of the in-zinerator concept
candidates.notes: Sandia National Laboratories technical report (November 2006 original, updated October 2007). Describes Z-pinch fusion-fission hybrid: 20 MW fusion → 3,000 MWth = 150x amplification. This is the primary Sandia source underlying the Apeiron I fission amplification claim referenced in the Not Boring article. Full text accessible via OSTI.

candidates.title: Z-Pinch-Driven Fusion-Fission Hybrids for Nuclear Waste Transmutation
candidates.notes: Related conference paper on same topic with direct PDF access at osti.gov/servlets/purl/1142686. Not extracted separately — the biblio/895981 technical report is the primary reference.

candidates.title: Fusion transmutation of waste: design and analysis of the in-zinerator concept (Academia.edu)
candidates.notes: Same report as OSTI 895981 — skipped in favor of official OSTI version.

gaps_attempted.notes: In-Zinerator technical report is the Sandia source underlying the 150x fission amplification claim. The 20 MW fusion → 3,000 MWth figure (ratio = 150) directly corresponds to the claim referenced in the analysis. This provides the independent technical basis for evaluating the Apeiron I claim beyond the Not Boring summary.

summary.notes: G-12 (Apeiron In-Zinerator) fully closed with Sandia OSTI report. G-1/G-11 partially addressed by arXiv AMPS paper covering DS physics scaling — no public cost model for IMG driver found. G-10 partially addressed by Frontiers materials survey (up to ~850K, not 900K+ specifically). G-6 remains unresolved — driver capital cost data is proprietary. G-13 skipped due to budget; existing iter-03 source already covers current public status.
